Finally, another large expense will involve the construction of testing bunkers to manage the significant high energy radiation emitting from the structures during conditioning. Foundation reinforcements and bunker construction is expected to total approximately $1M fully permitted while facility infrastructure expenses will amount to another $1M for facility water, heat exchangers, power, climate control and control room buildout. It is expected that at a rate of conditioning one structure per month, two power stations and associated equipment will be required with many spares on hand to minimize schedule risk. Included in the spares list would be another full RF power station. This will result in a total of roughly ~$12M for the high power testing facility required. Two Senior Scientists and two junior scientists are expected for these roles and can also service the needs of other RF based duties such as cold testing. 4 trained technical staff for system hookup and preparation and exchanging, along with infrastructure maintenance are envisioned. Additionally 1 dedicated operator per shift for 24 hour operation is expected although human factors may suggest that two would be better. All in, the staffing levels are not expected to be high in this facility and should be shared if possible with other departments. Although the average wages would be higher, due to the lower levels a monthly expense of ~$250k including OH/GA/benefits seems reasonable. If administrative, IT and facilities maintenance staff are required due to a stand alone facility, this could add another $50-60k per month. B.4.3 ES&H Environmental, Safety and Health consideration for this facility will primarily revolve around radiation safety monitoring and compliance requirements. Requirements for shielding, access barriers, dose monitoring and record keeping at the facility and individual level, establishment of procedures and training and active interlock systems are well known and important to adhere to. High voltage and currents, along with heavy lifting and material handling dangers will exist within this facility and extensive training, interlocks, lockout tagout and safety equipment will be required.
